body:
Reply with plain text only, no JSON, no preamble, and do not send messages to anyone else. Do not ask questions; decide.

You are drafting short Narrator lines for a Halloween D&D video game, "The Crooked Moon". The Narrator is the Vagrant, the green-skinned ferryman of a ghost train, telling the tale afterwards in a folksy Southern drawl. This batch is set in the Crooked House, a haunted manor on a hill above the village of Wickermoor: a house that warps itself, built on old dark power. A storm has shut the party inside. Here the Vagrant's humour is gone. He is hushed, dry and dead level, the drawl stripped down to bare bones, with silences in it. Never a joke, never a gloat; the dead are respected.

Rules every line follows:
- Second person ("you"), present tense. Never use any name, never the word {name}; the line is for whoever walks up, any hero.
- One or two sentences, under about 30 words in all. The second sentence is usually the turn or the payoff.
- Concrete senses (a smell, a sound, a temperature) over adjectives. No game words (no HP, roll, check, level, search, DC, saving throw, class names). Never tell the player what to feel. Never "suddenly". No modern slang. No winks at the player.
- No facts the party has not earned: only what a person standing in front of the thing could see, smell, hear or touch. Use only the facts given for each key; do not invent new people, places, monsters, props, objects or history. Do not name any real-world place.
- Drop a final g ("hangin'", "creakin'") in about one line in three, not more, and use no other dialect spelling (reckon, ain't and folks are fine, sparingly). The fiddle is never written or mentioned.
- Plain punctuation only: commas, full stops, hyphens, apostrophes, quotation marks. No em dashes, no semicolons, no brackets, no backticks, no stage directions, no placeholders other than where a key below says an EXTRA line may use {name}.
- Do not repeat an image in neighbouring keys. The house's palette, to spread across the lines, one or two details per line, not all at once: sepia rot and mildew green, faded rose and teal wallpaper, bruised purple upholstery, cracked tile, cobweb grey, dust and mildew; nothing square (doors that are trapezoids, frames that lean, floors that slope, a bulging turret); weasels scratching inside every wall; teeth clicking underfoot; a clock ticking somewhere; the storm; windows sealed and black, streaked with rain, lit by lightning. Sweet rot is the smell of the dining room only, burnt flesh the smell of the kitchen only, copper the smell of the bathroom only. The rooms are unlit unless the party brings light.

Output format, nothing else: for each key, a block exactly like

KEY enter:h2_foyer
PLAIN: the line
PLAIN2: a second plain line (only when the key says so)
EXTRA [class:bard]: the extra line (only when the key says so; this one may begin with {name} and say what that hero does or notices; it must still make sense alone)

Every key needs its PLAIN line, which must stand alone for any hero.
BATCH B2: EXAMINE LINES (bathroom to the attic). One block per key, PLAIN only unless an EXTRA is named. Each line says what the thing is and what it implies; the second sentence is the payoff or the unease. Where a key says "the fight begins", the line is the last quiet look before trouble, so tilt toward it without naming a monster or saying what happens next. Never give away who is really who in the cauldron room.

KEY examine:h11_tub
Facts: a claw-foot tub stained red to the rim, warm water or something like it still, steam on the mouldy tile, the smell of copper. The fight begins when you lean over it, so end on the surface of the water moving.

KEY examine:h11_door
Facts: the bathroom door, a trapezoid that hardly fits its frame, swollen wood, a tarnished knob. EXTRA [class:rogue]: starts with {name}, about the lock.

KEY examine:h12_bed
Facts: a canopy bed, curtains torn to ribbons, covers heaped and heaving as if something sleeps badly beneath them. Small white teeth lie scattered through the sheets. The fight begins when you pull the covers back, so end on the heaving.

KEY examine:h12_journal
Facts: a black leather journal on the desk, gilt monogram worn almost smooth, a small brass clasp. It is locked.

KEY examine:h12_balcony_doors
Facts: double doors of black glass at the end of the room, a brass catch crusted green, rain running down the other side.

KEY examine:h12_scratchings
Facts: long gouges in the plaster behind the bed, in bunches of four, as if by fingernails. Some are far too low down for a grown hand.

KEY examine:h13_crib
Facts: a mahogany crib, the rails riddled with tiny holes like pinpricks, a small threadbare blue teddy bear in the corner of the mattress, stuffed toys on a shelf above. The fight begins when you take the bear, so end on a toy's eye catching the light.

KEY examine:h14_cart
Facts: a liquor cart under cobweb, decanters furred with dust, and on the lower shelf four small stoppered vials that are strangely clean.

KEY examine:h14_tome
Facts: a heavy tome on a stand, cracked leather, the page edges brown, pages half covered in cramped ink and half empty.

KEY examine:h14_desk
Facts: a writing desk with a tall stack of books on it, a dry inkwell, a pen gone stiff, deep claw marks in the leather top.

KEY examine:h15_trapdoor
Facts: a square seam in the ceiling plaster with an iron ring set in it, grey with age. The air near it hums faintly. Touching it starts a roar that you feel in your teeth, so end on the first low note.

KEY examine:h15_bear
Facts: a very large brown bear mounted on its hind legs, claws raised, glass eyes. The seams along its chest and throat are stitched finer than any other mount in the room.

KEY examine:h15_trophy_crow
Facts: a stuffed black crow on a high shelf, wings half spread, one glass eye catching your light, dull feathers under dust.

KEY examine:h16_runes
Facts: runes cut deep into the walls, floor and ceiling, glowing blood-red and pulsing slowly. Six empty circles are cut among them, each about the size of a hand.

KEY examine:h17_cauldron
Facts: a great iron cauldron of glowing red liquid, steaming. Where it has slopped over the lip the floor has been eaten into pits. Teeth lie thick around its feet.

KEY examine:h17_phillip
Facts: a man in a fine suit bound beside the cauldron, head lolling, feverish, breathing shallowly.

KEY examine:h17_adela
Facts: a cloaked figure, hood forward, swaying on the spot like a reed, taking no step and making no sound.

KEY examine:h17_scratchings
Facts: scratchings on the wall, crude letters cut in a cramped furious hand, two names repeated over and over. Do not give the names.
result:
KEY examine:h11_tub
PLAIN: Warm steam curls off the mouldy tile, thick with the smell of copper from a claw-foot tub stained red to the rim. You lean over, and the dark surface shifts.

KEY examine:h11_door
PLAIN: Swollen wood cut into a trapezoid barely fits the leaning frame. Your hand finds the tarnished knob, cold and damp.
EXTRA [class:rogue]: {name} crouches by the tarnished latch, findin' the lock rusted solid from the inside.

KEY examine:h12_bed
PLAIN: Torn curtains hang in ribbons around sheets scattered with small white teeth. Beneath the heaped covers, something rises and falls in a heavy, restless heave.

KEY examine:h12_journal
PLAIN: A black leather journal rests on the desk, its gilt monogram worn nearly smooth by someone's thumb. A small brass clasp holds it shut tight.

KEY examine:h12_balcony_doors
PLAIN: Double doors of black glass stand sealed at the end of the room, the brass catch crusted green. Rain runs in cold, silent sheets down the other side.

KEY examine:h12_scratchings
PLAIN: Long gouges score the plaster behind the bed, four in a row where fingernails dragged down. The lowest marks sit scarce a foot off the floor.

KEY examine:h13_crib
PLAIN: A threadbare blue bear sits in the corner of a mahogany crib, its rails riddled with tiny pinprick holes. As you reach in, a stuffed toy on the shelf above catches your light in its glass eye.

KEY examine:h14_cart
PLAIN: Cobweb drapes a liquor cart and its dust-furred decanters. Down on the lower shelf, four small stoppered vials sit wiped clean.

KEY examine:h14_tome
PLAIN: A heavy tome rests on a stand in cracked leather, its brown-edged pages half choked with cramped ink. The rest lie blank, waitin' for a hand that never came back.

KEY examine:h14_desk
PLAIN: A tall stack of books crowds a writing desk beside a dry inkwell and a pen gone stiff. Deep claw marks tear right through the leather top.

KEY examine:h15_trapdoor
PLAIN: An age-grey iron ring hangs from a square seam in the ceiling plaster, the air around it hummin' low. When your fingers brush the cold metal, a deep vibration starts up in your teeth.

KEY examine:h15_bear
PLAIN: A great brown bear rears up on its hind legs, claws raised and glass eyes dull. Along its throat and chest, the seams are stitched finer than any other mount in the room.

KEY examine:h15_trophy_crow
PLAIN: High on a shelf, a stuffed black crow holds its dusty wings half spread. One glass eye takes your light and keeps it.

KEY examine:h16_runes
PLAIN: Runes cut deep into floor, wall, and ceiling pulse slow with a blood-red glow. Six empty circles sit carved among them, each the size of an open hand.

KEY examine:h17_cauldron
PLAIN: Glowing red liquid steams in a great iron pot, eatin' pits into the floorboards where it slopped over the lip. Teeth lie thick around its iron feet, clicking under your boots.

KEY examine:h17_phillip
PLAIN: A man in a fine suit slumps bound beside the iron pot, his head lolling on his chest. Heat comes off his skin in shallow, ragged breaths.

KEY examine:h17_adela
PLAIN: A figure stands with hood drawn forward, swaying on the spot like a dry reed. Not a step, not a breath, not a sound comes from beneath the cloak.

KEY examine:h17_scratchings
PLAIN: Crude letters score the wall in a cramped, furious hand. Two names are carved over and over until the plaster gives way to bare lath.
